newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier but above recent low.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier but above recent low.

text.p: Precious metals prices were narrowly mixed in European business on Thursday after gold had its lowest fixing since October 1993 on Wednesday morning.
But the tone remained bearish overall with the prospect of further central bank gold sales keeping the market cowed, traders said.
Gold was fixed at $353.05 per ounce after $354.00 in the morning and $354.45 previously. Wendesday morning's fix of $352.45 was the lowest since October 4, 1993.
"There might be a maximum of four dollars on the upside in this market. Between $356-$358 is where to sell," a dealer said.
In a fairly quiet New York market, Comex's February contract was $1.00 ahead just before the bullion fixing at $354.20 having pushed higher earlier.

Gold had a mixed ride since London's Wednesday close, after which dollar strength weakened values in New York before it picked up in Hong Kong on a combination of late buying from Japan, physical offtake and early short covering from Europe.
"There has been some producer selling but there is no real interest to buy other than short covering. Physical interest at these levels has been nothing special," a dealer said.
Gold has been hovering over steep falls all week.
Weakness was triggered by news on Monday that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold from reserves.

The news initially lifted some of the market despondency created by long-running rumours that a central bank had been selling bullion. But the fear of further central bank dishoarding quickly sent the price tumbling.
"I still think we are heading towards $340, although not necessarily in a straight line," one dealer said.
Independent technical analyst Brian Marber in his latest newsletter issued today advised clients to short gold.
He said a recent head and shoulders top formation on the charts implied a no time limit decline to $348.00 which offered potential support and was the place to take profits.
The other precious metals were very quiet as gold continued to hold centre stage in the complex.
Palladium was about $1.15 firmer at $120.25/$121.25 off earlier highs and reflecting the continuing silence from Moscow over opening talks with Japan for 1997's platinum group exports.
Platinum was less influenced by the Russian issue and was indicated at $359.25/$360.25, down about 65 cents on the close.
Silver was a couple of cents ahead at $4.71/$4.73.
